answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (Brady Hot Springs PoroTomo DAS, March 2016):

RECORDS
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, window 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, covering 3.314% of the time)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 detections above the catalogue completeness magnitude Mc)
- Pumping context: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED probability — catalogue-based (Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5, LBNL catalogue magnitudes; this is the calibrated one):
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND — uncalibrated DAS magnitudes, every detection counted as an event at/above catalogue Mc, so it over-counts (this is the upper bound, NOT calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated (LBNL catalogue) estimate of a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event is at most ~1.5e-2 per year even for the lowest b = 0.65 scenario (and ~1.2e-4/yr at b = 1.0), while the DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr over-counts because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all detections are treated as catalogue-complete events. The data show no strong anomaly pointing to injection-induced seismicity of Pohang scale; the calibrated probability is the one to trust.
